items.title: Alex Murdaugh Claims Investigator Lied About Evidence in Wife and Son’s Murders
items.summary:
Alex Murdaugh ’s lawyers are alleging that the lead investigator in his wife, Maggie Murdaugh , and their son Paul Murdaugh ’s murder case lied about evidence during his first trial,

During a Friday, November 13, pretrial hearing, Murdaugh’s attorneys and prosecutors presented their latest arguments in front of Circuit Judge Debra McCaslin while requesting the court dismiss the murder indictment against the disgraced former lawyer.

Alex’s attorneys asked the court to dismiss the indictment against him “without prejudice,” claiming that former lead State Law Enforcement Division (SLED) Investigator David Owen lied while testifying before the Colleton County grand jury in 2022, according to the ABC 11 .

After his attorneys asked that his murder indictment be dropped, McCaslin said she would try to get a written order on the dismissal request finished by Friday, November 20, according to WCSC . However, she did not rule on the request during the most recent hearing.

What Was Alex Murdaugh's Sentence Before His Convictions Were Overturned? 

Alex, 58, was convicted in 2023 of fatally shooting Maggie, 52, and Paul, 22, on their property in South Carolina on June 7, 2021.

The once-prominent lawyer appealed the double-murder conviction, and the South Carolina Supreme Court overturned his convictions in May . The court then ordered that he receive a new trial after it was determined that former Colleton County Clerk of Court Becky Hill improperly influenced jurors during the initial court proceedings.

“The Lafourche Parish Sheriff’s Office continues to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death of Kenan Urker,” the sheriff’s office told Us in a Monday, November 15, statement. “While we understand the Lafourche Parish Coroner’s Office has released updated information regarding the cause of death, our investigation is separate and remains ongoing.”

Authorities added, “At this time, we have no additional information to release. We will provide an update when we reach a point in the investigation where additional information can be shared.”

The sheriff’s statement comes shortly after the Lafourche Parish Coroner’s Office confirmed on Monday that Urker’s death last month was the result of an accidental drug overdose .

Gypsy Rose Blanchard's Ex Ken Urker's Cause of Death Revealed

News broke in October that Blanchard’s ex-fiancé was found dead inside a Louisiana home on his 34th birthday. At the time, foul play was not suspected.

Urker — who is survived by his and Blanchard’s 22-month-old daughter, Aurora — met Blanchard, 35, in 2017 as prison pen pals. At the time, Blanchard was incarcerated for her role in the 2015 murder of her mother, Clauddine “Dee Dee” Blanchard .

Investigators rescued baby Koah Sharp after he survived an estimated 24 hours inside of a crate wrapped in a towel that was unearthed not far from his grandfather’s home in Batesburg-Leesville, South Carolina, on Tuesday, November 10, according to Lexington County authorities.

In her first interview, Koah’s mother, Dezarae Sharp , spoke with the New York Times on Friday, November 13, describing her disbelief over what allegedly occurred.

Michael Comer , Koah’s father and Dezarae’s ex-boyfriend, is charged with attempted murder, unlawful conduct toward a child, custodial interference and burglary, court records show.

“I didn’t think he could go that far,” Sharp said of Comer while speaking with the New York Times .

Comer allegedly took Koah when the boy was in the care of Comer’s mother on Monday, November 9, resulting in an urgent search near Batesburg-Leesville.

Comer was located later that evening at a local outbuilding, without Koah, and taken into custody on a burglary charge, according to authorities.

The star defensive end tore his ACL in his right knee and will miss the rest of the season, ESPN reported on Monday, November 16. The Lions have yet to make an official announcement regarding Hutchinson’s status.  

Hutchinson reportedly received an MRI in Germany and will undergo additional tests in the United States upon his arrival.

items.title: When Is Lindsay Clancy's New Trial? Retrial Date Set by Judge, More Updates

Lindsay Clancy is heading back to court, and Judge William Sullivan has set a new trial date of March 29, 2027, for the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three children. The decision was made weeks after the judge denied her legal team’s attempt to dismiss the murder charges altogether.

Clancy appeared in Plymouth Superior Court on November 16, 2026, to discuss the future of her case after her September 2026 mistrial, with prosecutors using the hearing to formally share their plans to retry her. 

When Is Lindsay Clancy’s New Trial? 
 The commonwealth pushed for a retrial to begin in May 2027, but Sullivan opted for an earlier March 2027 date . The judge has previously announced plans to retire in 2027.

Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz holds the ultimate authority over how Clancy is charged the second time around. Cruz has the power to retry her on first-degree murder — the same charge she faced in the first trial — or to pursue a lesser charge, such as second-degree murder or manslaughter.

Can Lindsay Clancy's Defense Team Claim Double Jeopardy After Mistrial? 

The scheduling decision marked the latest in a series of rulings Sullivan has issued since the previous hearing on November 9, 2026, when he denied Clancy’s motion to dismiss the murder charges tied to the deaths of her children: Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, in January 2023.

Leading up to the new trial are pretrial hearings on December 30, 2026, and February 18, 2027.

items.summary:
Kirk Cousins was noticeably overcome by the moment following a dominant win over the Green Bay Packers in his return to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, November 15.  

“It was emotional coming to the stadium,” Cousins, 38, told ESPN’s Lindsey Thiry on the field at Green Bay’s Lambeau Field after the Vikings’ 30-10 victory. “Three years ago, tearing my Achilles here. It’s been a tough three years. I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today, and grateful for my teammates and what they did to make this outcome possible.” 

Cousins was traded back to the Vikings from the Las Vegas Raiders on Wednesday, November 11. 

The quarterback previously played for Minnesota for six seasons from 2018 to 2023. His final game as a member of the Vikings came in October 2023, when he tore his right Achilles tendon in a game against the Packers. Cousins spent the next two seasons with the Atlanta Falcons before signing with the Raiders in April.  

Kirk Cousins’ Wife Julie Reacts to Trade Back to the Minnesota Vikings 

While acknowledging the symbolism of the moment, Cousins urged, “There’s so much football up ahead.” 

“Certainly it’s gratifying to be able to come back here with the purple on,” Cousins added. “I think to come back here with another team isn’t quite the same. To come back here with the purple on, similar time of year, three years later, it’s a blessing, to be able to have a win like we had today.”

items.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
items.summary:
After years of celebrity interviews, I have learned not to be fooled by the allure of fame. We never really know them – we know what they want us to know

As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.

I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.

Continue reading...
items.t: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood

items.title: Two courtrooms, one celebrity: how did the Russell Brand case compare with the rape trial next door?

What is going on inside Russell Brand’s head as he arrives at court for the start of his rape trial? He sees the dozens of cameras and journalists lined outside Southwark crown court, many of whom have been waiting since before 7am, and he tells himself that the media are all against him. “It seems to me that they believe that I am guilty, and that this should be the rubber-stamping of the process of my destruction.”

He walks with his wife, Laura, and his bodyguard past the photographers, “clickering, clackering, snickering paparazzi, like locusts, peculiar concoctions, not fully humans”, and up into the court, where he is suddenly overwhelmed by “the presence of something very beautiful, grace”. “In a situation like I’m in, it’s impossible not to turn to God. Truth and justice are the only things that can save me,” he thinks.
